status: DESCRIPTIVE — CAP-112 16-TAG DECOMPOSITION; NO TARGET, FREEZE, GRANT OR A1 CELL
question: What keeps the ten failing 16-tag seeds below A=60 at prediction cap 112: A rank, support eligibility, or edge family?
definition: Per-candidate A membership and best returned rank at cap 112 and at a diagnostic cap 1000, K membership, acquisition support, cell relation and old/new family for the ten 16-tag seeds that fail joint C1 at loop cap 120 / prediction cap 112.
method: One no-arm replay per seed and cap. A_rank is the minimum 1-based position in the returned list. Cap-112 A/K counts must match the committed cap-112 artifact exactly. Cap 1000 is diagnostic only.
reading: All 69 A-missing candidate edges across the ten failing seeds appear at diagnostic cap 1000, at ranks 65-189. They are support-eligible and all 69 are transition candidates; none is a cooccurrence. 62/69 are flip_q. The cap-112 run excludes them, but cap 1000 also changes which predictions are reinforced across cycles, so the rank range is diagnostic, not a fixed cutoff. The stable discriminator is the edge family: flip_q transitions are ranked out of the 112-row prediction window. The gap survives at matched support 16+: flip_p is 311/318 (97.8%) A against flip_q 149/182 (81.9%).
not_evidence: A descriptive decomposition of ten no-arm 16-tag seeds at one cap pair plus a diagnostic ceiling. Cap 1000 changes reinforcement across cycles, so it locates missing edges but is not a pure window expansion. It does not establish why flip_q transitions rank lower, and it is not a treatment, target-viability or successor result.
